# DRAFT: Medical device adverse incident report

> This is a draft for human review. It has not been submitted. A manufacturer would report
> through the MHRA MORE portal; healthcare professionals and users report through the Yellow Card scheme.

## 1. Device
- Name: ClinicDrift-monitored DR screening model
- Version: v1.0
- Intended use: screening retinal photographs for referable diabetic retinopathy

## 2. Where and when
- Clinic: IN-APT-02 (India)
- Period: week 1 (starting 2026-01-05)

## 3. What happened
ClinicDrift found that this clinic's scans no longer resemble the scans on which the AI was validated (drift score 0.99, where 0.5 means like training and 1 clearly different).
Consequently, the catch rate (sensitivity for referable disease) cannot be verified from 50 scans from this week, and expert grades for these scans have not yet been received. The AI is referring more patients than usual: 82% of this week's scans, compared with 68% of the training scans.

## 4. Potential patient impact
Because the catch rate cannot be verified, the number of possibly missed cases is not estimated. No patient harm has been confirmed.

## 5. Likely cause
The clinic is producing significantly lower resolution and poorer quality images compared with the training data, which affects feature extraction and leads to an elevated referral rate. (category: camera or image quality; confidence 95%; source: gemini)

Evidence:
- Drift score of 0.99 indicating scans do not look like training data
- Mean quality dropped from 0.5 to 0.108 with a relative change of -0.784
- Mean resolution dropped from 1020.0 px to 224.0 px with a relative change of -0.781
- Mean sharpness dropped from 0.000399 to 6.86e-05 with a relative change of -0.828
- Mean contrast dropped from 0.0963 to 0.0648 with a relative change of -0.327
- Mean brightness dropped from 0.373 to 0.298 with a relative change of -0.2
- Referral rate increased from 0.685 to 0.82 with a relative change of 0.198

## 6. Action
ClinicDrift paused the AI at this clinic because its scans have drifted beyond the data on which the AI was validated, meaning its catch rate cannot be verified. We recommend sending this clinic's scans for human grading until the checks below are complete.

Checks:
- [ ] Inspect camera hardware settings and ensure correct output resolution is selected
- [ ] Check lens cleanliness and focus mechanism of the retinal camera
- [ ] Verify proper ambient lighting and pupil dilation protocols at the clinic
- [ ] Review image export and compression pipelines to ensure downscaling is not corrupting scan quality

## 7. Regulatory context
- Post-market surveillance (PMS): this alarm is part of ongoing monitoring of the device in use.
- Predetermined change control plan (PCCP): any model change made in response should fall within an agreed PCCP.
- MHRA AI Airlock Phase 2 report: see recommendations 3 and 4.

## 8. MIT AI Risk Repository tags
- 7.3 AI system safety, failures & limitations > Lack of capability or robustness
- 1.3 Discrimination & toxicity > Unequal performance across groups
- 5.1 Human-computer interaction > Overreliance and unsafe use
